artery: a blood vessel carrying blood away from the heart
arteries: blood vessels carrying blood away from the heart
arterial: relating to the arteries or the blood they carry
veins: blood vessels carrying blood back toward the heart
venous: relating to the veins or the blood they carry
ventricle: a chamber of the heart that pumps blood out
auricles: the upper chambers of the heart that receive blood
valves: small flaps in the heart that let blood flow one way
cavity: a hollow space inside the body or an organ
cavities: hollow spaces inside the body or its organs
orifices: openings or mouths of tubes or vessels in the body
pellicles: thin skins or membranes covering something
rarefied: made thinner and less dense, as air or vapor is
ligature: a band or tie used to bind something tightly
spirits: subtle vital fluids thought to drive the body's movements
distilled: purified by heating a liquid into vapor and cooling it
consistency: the thickness or firmness of a substance
physician: a medical doctor who treats illness
brutes: animals, which the author believes lack reason
reasonings: chains of argument or logical reasoning
sceptics: people who doubt that real knowledge is possible
geometrical: relating to geometry or proofs made by geometry
algebra: a branch of mathematics using letters for unknown quantities
demonstrations: rigorous proofs that establish a conclusion beyond doubt
maxims: general principles guiding conduct or reasoning
precepts: rules or instructions for conduct or practice
judicious: showing good sense and sound judgment
discourse: a formal treatise or extended spoken or written account
tract: a short written treatise on a subject
endeavor: to try hard or make a serious effort
ancients: people of earlier ages, especially Greek and Roman writers
virtue: moral goodness and excellence of character
morals: principles of right and wrong conduct
poesy: poetry, or the art of writing verse
eloquence: skill and grace in speaking or writing persuasively
commodious: spacious and convenient for living or use
heavens: the sky, or the universe beyond the earth
chaos: a state of complete disorder without form or order
repugnant: distasteful, or contradictory to reason and belief
extravagant: absurdly excessive or beyond reasonable limits
intelligible: capable of being understood by the mind
corporeal: bodily or physical, as opposed to spiritual
compounded: formed by combining several parts together
alleged: claimed to be true without proof
existent: actually existing in the real world
thence: from that place or from that cause
scruple: a doubt or hesitation arising from conscience
affections: emotions, feelings, or inclinations of the mind
fancied: imagined or supposed, often without good grounds
entertain: to hold a thought or opinion in the mind
